# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–4 (Complete and Final – Updated 61)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford; Also: Chiswick Mall (Miss Pinkerton's academy), Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, playground with tree and broken glass on wall
- **Current Setting Details**: River crossing at Gulton and Quenwick; forge with chalked crooked sun on wall; wind from water with salt and tar smell; gulls quarreling over fish heads by steps; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; frost silvering hedges overnight; turnip cart passing well; light going early as spring approaches; children chasing hoop down lane; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; market town of Bryngate; hill farms of Coldcombe and Mirecombe; bees humming in lavender behind parsonage; bell for vespers ringing thinly across roofs; rain threatening but holding off; front room on second floor with chintz tent hung round with rich India pattern and double calico of tender rose-colour, featherbed with two pillows; back drawing-room with piano situated in darkness; schoolyard with tree where Arabian Nights may be read in solitude

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return to Middlemarch; now married with infant son
- **Family Reconciliation**: Initial opposition resolved; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea and Will's cousins enjoy playing with visiting children
- **Sir James's Opposition**: Never ceased regarding second marriage as mistake; tradition in Middlemarch that she married sickly clergyman then within year gave up estate to marry propertyless cousin
- **Dorothea's Life Assessment**: Acts not ideally beautiful but mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive; growing good of world partly dependent on unhistoric acts

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- **Present Status**: Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window
- **Marriage Achievement**: Solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations
- **Fred's Development**: Remains steady; told Mary happiness half owing to Farebrother; never wholly free from misled hopefulness but gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner
- **Fred's Feelings**: Had pleasant vision of bright hearth; told Mary magnanimously Farebrother was worthier; sorry for other men who could not have Mary
- **Children**: Three boys only; youngest resembles grandfather; minimal formal teaching but children found quite forward at school

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)**
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; dressed in white with bare shoulders; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist; sings better than Amelia
- **Departure from Chiswick**: Said French farewell to Miss Pinkerton; threw Dixonary at Miss Jemima; sank back in easy frame of mind; nobody cried for her leaving
- **Character**: Had dismal precocity of poverty; showed no will rivaling Miss Pinkerton's; never had been a girl, was woman since age eight; determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed in life since age eight when caught stealing jam by godmother; capable of calculated charm and intimacy; actually blushed when appearing before Joseph and Osborne with ringlets bent over knitting; inquired about Joseph's purse
- **Position Obtained**: Miss Pinkerton recommended her for governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family after months-long battle to cancel indentures; Miss Pinkerton stated "I cannot find fault with Miss Sharp's conduct except to myself; must allow her talents and accomplishments are of high order"; petition for extension of leave already despatched before winter; difficult to find pretext for abruptly dismissing her
- **Crisp Affair**: Reverend Mr. Crisp, fresh from Oxford and curate to Vicar Flowerdew of Chiswick, fell in love and proposed in intercepted note; **rumor claims** tart-woman hinted great deal more than public knowledge; Mrs. Crisp summoned him from Buxton; truth of his letter unknown
- **At Sedley Household**: Invited by friend Miss Sedley for week before governess duties; Amelia showed her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl brought from India by brother Joseph; won over entire household through charming behavior
- **Regarding Joseph Sedley**: Upon learning of India shawls, Rebecca determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"; redoubled caresses to Amelia; vowed never to part with white cornelian necklace
- **Meeting Joseph**: Went downstairs with arm round Amelia's waist; agitated at drawing-room door; dressed in white with bare shoulders as white as snow
- **At Dinner**: Thought she must be quiet about India; at chili, laid down fork crying "Water, for Heaven's sake, water!"; swallowed mortification, made comical good-humoured air about Arabian Nights, cream-tarts, and cayenne
- **Joseph's Panic**: During two or three days following dinner, Joseph did not visit house nor mention Miss Rebecca's name; Miss Rebecca was respectful to Mrs. Sedley, delighted at Bazaars, wheeled to theatre by Mrs. Sedley
- **Amelia's Support**: When Amelia had headache and could not attend pleasure party, Rebecca refused to go without her, saying "What! you who have shown the poor orphan what happiness and love are for the first time in her life--quit YOU? Never!"; green eyes filled with tears; Mrs. Sedley found her charming
- **Winning Over Household**: Laughed at Mr. Sedley's jokes with cordiality pleasing to that good-natured gentleman; interested Mrs. Blenkinsop in raspberry-jam preserving; called Sambo "Sir" and "Mr. Sambo" delighting him; apologized to lady's maid with sweetness and humility; charmed both Drawing Room and Servants' Hall
- **Familiarity with Family**: By day ten of stay, on footing of considerable familiarity with family; Amelia loved her like sister
- **Hand Pressure Incident**: Gave Joseph gentle pressure with little hand, drew it back frightened, looked in his face then down at carpet-rods; Joseph's heart thumped at involuntary, timid motion of regard
- **Joseph's Feelings Rekindled**: Joseph thought "I exactly begin to feel as I did at Dumdum with Miss Cutler"; made many sweet appeals to Rebecca about dinner dishes
- **Vauxhall Plan**: Amelia reminded Joseph of Easter promise to take her to Vauxhall, proposing Rebecca should go with them now; **actual outcome**: Thunderstorm on evening appointed for Vauxhall party prevented attendance; young people remained at home instead and declared themselves rather glad of storm than otherwise
- **Intimate Evening at Home**: Left alone with Joseph Sedley in drawing-room while Amelia and George Osborne went to piano in back drawing-room; Rebecca occupied in knitting green silk purse; conversation with Joseph established great confidence and intimacy; talk carried on in low, becoming tone; asked Joseph about purse recipient; Joseph spoke of dangers of tiger-hunts being pleasanter, described only once being hunted and nearly killed by fright; Joseph grew bold and asked "For whom she was knitting the green silk purse?"; Rebecca replied "For any one who wants a purse" in gentle winning way; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music from other room ended, blushed, blew nose in agitation; lay awake thinking delightfully of songs after Cutcherry, distinguished girl, her French superior to Governor-General's lady, sensation she would make at Calcutta balls; concluded "It's evident the poor devil's in love with me"; thought of marrying her, saying "I might go farther, and fare worse"; fell asleep in these meditations
- **Next Morning**: Upon Joseph's next visit to Russell Square before luncheon (first such honour), Rebecca was employed on knitting work; when Joseph's buggy arrived, knowing glances telegraphed between Osborne and Amelia; pair smiled archly at Rebecca who blushed as she bent fair ringlets over knitting; heart beat rapidly as Joseph appeared puffing from stairs in shining creaking boots, new red waistcoat, blushing behind wadded neckcloth; Joseph presented nosegays of flowers from Covent Garden Market purchased that morning, one to each young woman with solemn bow; Rebecca exclaimed "O heavenly, heavenly flowers!" and smelt them delicately, held to bosom, cast eyes to ceiling in ecstasy; looked first into bouquet to see if billet-doux hidden but found no letter
- **Pine-apple Incident**: Joseph stated he bought flowers at Nathan's and pine-apple given to Sambo for tiffin; Rebecca said she had never tasted pine and longed beyond everything to taste one; conversation continued while Osborne left room and Amelia went presumably to superintend slicing of pine-apple; Jos left alone with Rebecca who resumed work with green silk and shining needles quivering rapidly under white slender fingers
- **Current Moment (Excerpt 538)**: Rebecca refuses Joseph's request to sing, citing low spirits; asks him to help finish green silk purse; Joseph seated tete-a-tete looking at her with killing expression, arms stretched out in imploring attitude, hands bound in web of green silk which she unwinds

**Joseph Sedley**
- **Position and Background**: In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint and returned to Europe; does not live with family but has own lodgings like gay young bachelor
- **Appearance and Habits**: Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres, appears at opera; at home in morning costume of those days' dandy; extremely talkative in man's society
- **Initial Reaction to Rebecca**: Bounced off arm-chair at her appearance, blushed excessively, hid face in neckcloths, continued huge clattering at poker and tongs, said "For heaven's sake see if my buggy's at the door. I CAN'T wait. I must go"
- **Entertainment and Sleep**: Burst out laughing at Rebecca's chili incident; fell asleep during dinner story; tells Indian stories repeatedly
- **Indulgences After Dinner**: Contented himself with bottle of claret besides Madeira at dinner; ate couple plates of strawberries and cream and twenty-four little rout cakes; thought great deal about girl upstairs; noticed her drop handkerchief twice at dinner; drank fitting quantity of port-wine tete-a-tete with George Osborne in dining-room during thunderstorm evening
- **Cowardice**: Nearly cried with vexation at father's joke about ordering elephant from Exeter 'Change; father stopped joking and offered champagne saying "It's all fair on the Stock Exchange, Jos"
- **Escape to Theatre**: Slipped away on pointed toes of his boots to see Forty Thieves and Miss Decamp's dance without waking father
- **Prediction re Rebecca**: Destined to be prey to woman as father goes on 'Change daily; first woman who fishes for him will hook him

**Miss Amelia Sedley**
- **Character**: Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; friends with Miss Sharp; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister after ten days; has natural infirmity of tears, described as defect of "silly little thing"; match-maker at heart; would have been delighted if Joseph carried back wife to India; warmed into most tender friendship for Rebecca in course of few days' constant intercourse
- **Discovery of Rebecca's Virtues**: Discovered a million of virtues and amiable qualities in Rebecca which she had not perceived at Chiswick; affection of young ladies grows rapid as Jack's bean-stalk reaching sky in night; after marriage this yearning after Ideal subsides as women centre affections on husbands and children
- **Family Connections**: Brother Joseph (collector); godson George Osborne (family friend for twenty-three years); parents Mr. and Mrs. Sedley
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; fell in love or appeared to fall in love with George Osborne at single instant when he asked her for music; went with him to piano in back drawing-room; put hand into his in darkness, ostensibly so he could guide her among chairs and ottomans; was writing to twelve dearest friends at Chiswick Mall when Joseph arrived next morning
- **Possessions**: White cornelian necklace, Cashmere shawls, sprigged muslin, embroidered beautiful pair of braces for brother Joseph; wrote note to George Osborne on Twelfth-night previously (misspelled "twelfth" without the "f")

**George Osborne**
- **Background and Family Connection**: Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; received silver cup at six weeks old from John Sedley; received coral with gold whistle and bells at six months; regularly "tipped" at Christmas by old gentleman; thrashed by Joseph Sedley when latter was hobbadyhoy and George was impudent urchin of ten years old; as familiar with family as daily acts of kindness and intercourse could make him
- **Character and Feelings**: Clever artist; at comfortable evening during thunderstorm, did not seem least disappointed at Vauxhall cancellation; felt extraordinary, almost irresistible impulse to seize Amelia in arms and kiss her in face of company; hinted he should like to sit in dark during piano performance; somehow already present at Russell Square when Joseph arrived next morning; exchanged knowing glances with Amelia upon Joseph's arrival; smiled archly with her at Rebecca; departed from drawing-room during Rebecca's renewed knitting to allow her and Joseph privacy
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying Amelia; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with Amelia at single instant; went with her to piano in back drawing-room during thunderstorm evening; allowed her to put hand in his for guidance

**William Dobbin** [NEW CHARACTER - School Years]
- **Background**: Son of a merchant/grocer; father keeps shop, wife is grocer's wife living in back parlour in Thames Street
- **School Experience at Doctor Swishtail's Seminary**: Giant amongst boys, downcast and stupefied appearance, dog's-eared primer, tight corduroys; incapable of acquiring Latin rudiments from Eton Latin Grammar; continually "taken down" by small boys with pink faces and pinafores; mercilessly bullied by entire school; corduroys sewn up, bed-strings cut, buckets and benches upset to break his shins, parcels containing paternal soap and candles sent to him, subject of endless jesting; bore everything patiently, entirely dumb and miserable; compared unfavorably to Cuff and others
- **Defense of Fellow Student**: While reading Arabian Nights under tree in playground (seeking solitude and happiness), witnessed Cuff beating small boy who had been instructed to purchase rum-shrub beyond playground wall, foot had slipped, bottle broken, shrub spilt, pantaloons damaged; Dobbin sprang up and cried "Hold off, Cuff; don't bully that child any more; or I'll--" (response interrupted); previously had threatened Cuff with leaden inkstand when latter attempted to strike him for refusing to write to "old Mother Figs" (his mother), saying "Don't strike, or I'll THMASH you" with such wickedness that Cuff backed down; after that Cuff never meddled personally with Dobbin though always spoke of him with contempt behind his back
- **Character Assessment**: Generous boy; feels injustice acutely; shrinks before slight; has acute sense of wrong and glowing gratitude for kindness; foolish soul perhaps revolted against tyranny or harbored revenge against bully; patient, dumb, miserable demeanor belies deeper feelings

**Mr. Cuff** [NEW CHARACTER - School Bully]
- **Position and Character**: Great chief and dandy of Swishtail Seminary; unquestioned king of school ruling subjects with splendid superiority; smuggled wine; fought town-boys; had ponies for riding home Saturdays; owned top-boots for hunting holidays; possessed gold repeater; took snuff like Doctor; attended Opera, knew merits of principal actors (preferred Mr. Kean to Mr. Kemble); could knock off forty Latin verses in hour; could make French poetry; rumored Doctor himself feared him
- **Bullying Behavior**: Despised "Figs" (Dobbin) most, abused and sneered at him constantly, scarcely condescended to hold personal communication with him; forced other boys to black his shoes, toast his bread, fag out and give him balls at cricket during summer afternoons; beat small boys including one who failed rum-shrub errand; attempted to strike Dobbin but backed down when threatened with inkstand; thereafter spoke of Dobbin with contempt behind his back but never meddled personally with him again

## Minor Characters and Updates
- **Mr. Sedley**: Coarse man from Stock Exchange; jocular, good-natured gentleman
- **Mrs. Sedley**: Good-natured lady; conducted curtain lecture with husband regarding treatment of Joseph
- **Miss Pinkerton**, **Miss Jemima**, **Mrs. Blenkinsop**, **Sambo**, **Reverend Mr. Crisp**: As previously noted
- **Orlwood Family**: Fedette Orlwood hummed tune while scrubbing step, fell asleep in chair before fire caught (twice noted), spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; Madrek Orlwood counted coins twice coming up penny short, swore to Ilena to rebuild fallen wall at Fenmere and shook on it; Ilena Orlwood mentioned

## Rumors and Unverified Claims Preserved
- **School-Related**: Torture in public school licensed as knot in Russia; ungentlemanlike to resist it (narrative commentary)
- **Earlier Claims**: As previously noted regarding Crisp affair, blood debts, mill ledgers, fires, abbeys, deeds, buried treasures, chapel vaults, toll bridges
